title: Exercise 2: Add Fractions with Unlike Denominators
exerciseInfo: Practice adding fractions with unlike denominators by creating a common denominator, combining the numerators, and simplifying the result.
Arithmetic Level 2 is allowed. This permits nested sums and products, the negative unit, and simple nonnegative whole-number exponents.
To rewrite 2/3 with denominator 6, use multiplication by 1 and the inverse-product tools to create an equivalent fraction. Work out the needed factor and numerator yourself.
A displayed unit fraction such as 1/7 means inverse(7) itself, not a separate factor 1 multiplied by inverse(7). More generally, a/b is represented as a multiplied by inverse(b).
completionMessage: When the final fraction is in lowest terms, compare it with the original sum and make sure the value has not changed.

steps.label: Use a common denominator
guidance: The first fraction needs a denominator of 6. Determine which numerator will make the new fraction equivalent to 2/3.
Only the form of the first fraction should change; its value must stay the same.
